title: Verdigris Analytics POC: Goldset, Hallucination Goals and Benchmarking Scope
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 6-week POC focused on quality evaluation for Verdigris' document summarization and question-answering workflows. Agreed on golden prompt set, regression test patterns, hallucination detection heuristics, scoring rubric (precision/recall/format), target SLAs for latency and cost guardrails, and deliverables/timeline for benchmarks and pilot acceptance.
next_steps: Samira to share initial benchmarking spreadsheet and golden-prompt template by 2026-12-22
Ethan to provision sandbox endpoints and sample runbook for KV caching tests by 2026-12-29
Maya to deliver 500 labeled QA pairs + 200 edge-case documents by 2027-01-04
action_items: Samira Patel - Share benchmark sheet and example eval prompts - 2026-12-22
Ethan Liu - Temp sandbox endpoints + instructions for load generator - 2026-12-29
Maya Chen - Push labeled dataset to secure bucket (s3://vdg-poc-data) - 2027-01-04
Rajiv Kumar - Confirm VPC peering constraints and IP allowlist - 2026-12-21
Omar Farouk - Provide short SOC2/KMS checklist questions we should prep answers for - 2026-12-24
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-18 15:30 UTC — Duration ~54m
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Nora (Redwood CSM), Maya (Verdigris Head of ML), Rajiv (Lead Data Eng), Priya (PM), Omar (Security)

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for making time today, we'll keep this tight — main goal is to align on how we'll judge quality for the POC, the workload size, and the timelines. also want to surface any security blockers early.
[00:14] Maya: yeah thanks samira, we appreciate it. quick context — Verdigris runs an automated summarization + extractive QA pipeline for energy sector docs, very long PDFs, variable formatting. our main pain is hallucination in answers and inconsistent formatting in summaries.
[00:32] Rajiv: and to add, our production queries often have long context windows, we stitch together OCR outputs; token distribution is heavy on the left tail but occasionally we get 4k+ sequences. so throughput matters.
[00:48] Ethan: got it. from the Redwood side we'll propose a golden-prompt set that matches your top 10 user intents and edge cases for hallucinations. we usually do a 500-sample golden set for early runs, then expand to 2–3k for regression.
[01:07] Priya: so what do you mean by golden prompts exactly? like canonical system+user pairs?
[01:12] Ethan: yeah, canonical instructions, constrained output format, and a few variants to test robustness. e.g., prompt that demands bulletized answers with source citations, another that asks for concise 2-sentence summaries with numeric extraction.
[01:27] Maya: okay that maps. our acceptance criteria is strict: <5% hallucination on golden set, and formatting compliance >95% for summaries. does that sound feasible?
[01:38] Samira: it's ambitious but doable for a POC if we lock model family and constraints. we should define hallucination precisely — is it fabricated facts, wrong citations, or both?
[01:49] Omar: from security's POV, fabricated assertions tied to PII or regulated metrics are a compliance risk. we need audit logs and deterministic scoring so we can trace back failing prompts.
[02:03] Nora: we can enable token-level logging in the sandbox and provide the eval trace. we'll include trace IDs in the benchmark outputs.
[02:12] Rajiv: let's talk workload sizing — we estimate ~10k queries/day in steady-state for the pilot traffic shape, but for the POC bench runs we'd like to emulate 100–300 QPS bursts to check batching and KV cache effects.
[02:27] Ethan: perfect. for benchmarking we'll run three modes: cold-cache (no KV), warm-cache (typical prefix reuse), and steady-state (sustained arrival). we'll capture p95/p50 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens.
[02:41] Priya: can we also run a token-efficiency test across quantized variants? we might have constraints to run something on dedicated vs hosted.
[02:49] Samira: yes — Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles; for the POC we'll compare float16 baseline vs 4-bit quantized to get unit-cost delta. we'll include quality drop threshold — e.g., if ROUGE drops >3 points we flag.
[03:03] Maya: what about regression tests and golden set maintenance? we want automated checks so every deploy runs the suite.
[03:10] Ethan: we recommend a two-tier regression approach: 'critical' golden prompts (manual-reviewed, block release if failing) and 'monitoring' set (larger, statistical). critical set is ~150 prompts. monitoring set ~2k. CI integration via webhook or scheduled runs.
[03:26] Rajiv: how are hallucinations detected automatically? we don't have perfect ground truth for everything.
[03:31] Ethan: good point. detection is a hybrid: exact-match and fuzzy-match to ground truth for extractive tasks, plus heuristic checks for contradictions, unsupported numeric claims, and cross-referencing with document provenance (if answer cites a source that isn't in context we mark as hallucination). we also run a reverse-consistency check — ask the model to justify the answer and then check claims against source text. it's noisy but useful.
[03:58] Maya: hmm reverse-checking seems expensive. will that blow up latency?
[04:01] Ethan: in production we'd use it as an offline eval; for the POC we can run it on the golden set only. live use would be sampling-based.
[04:12] Priya: scoring approach — what metrics do you propose? precision/recall for QA, ROUGE/BERU for summaries? and a composite quality score?
[04:20] Ethan: yes. metric set: for QA — exact match (where applicable), F1, hallucination rate; for summaries — ROUGE-L, BERTScore, format-compliance rate; composite quality = weighted sum (we'll present a suggested weighting, e.g., 0.5 QA F1, 0.3 hallucination penalty, 0.2 format). weights should map to your product priorities.
[04:40] Samira: we'll include an expected acceptance threshold: composite >= 0.75 on the critical golden set and hallucination <= 5%. that's draft.
[04:50] Omar: security questions — you mentioned sandbox tokens/keys. will data leave our VPC?
[04:55] Ethan: for the POC we can do two modes: hosted sandbox (data encrypted at rest, SOC2) or private deployment with VPC peering. for initial bench runs, many customers do hosted but with strict token retention policies; if you need on-prem, that pushes timeline and contract work.
[05:14] Rajiv: timeline then — what are we looking at for a 6-week POC?
[05:18] Samira: proposed: week 0 (this week) align on datasets/prompts and security checklist; week 1–2: golden set creation + sandbox provisioning; week 3: run initial bench (cold/warm/steady) and quantify latency/cost; week 4: model tuning/quantization experiments + regression runs; week 5: run expanded monitoring set + hallucination analyses; week 6: joint review and acceptance decision.
[05:37] Maya: that works, though we need to schedule an internal stakeholder demo in week 5.
[05:41] Priya: regarding acceptance, besides composite score, we want a small user study (5 power users) verifying answer usefulness. can that be included?
[05:49] Samira: yes we can include a human-in-the-loop check as an acceptance criterion — we'll help design a 5-user rubric.
[05:55] Rajiv: on technical limits — we want to test KV cache behavior with long contexts; can you simulate 8k+ effective context by appending state?
[06:01] Ethan: yep we can stitch contexts. caveat: some models have hard tokenizer limits; we'll simulate by chunking and measuring end-to-end latency for retrieval+inference. we'll log KV hit/miss rates.
[06:12] Maya: one more — format checks. our downstream systems expect JSON with specific fields, if model emits malformed JSON it's a showstopper. what's your approach?
[06:21] Ethan: enforce structured-output schema and run parser checks as part of the eval. we'll flag format-compliance percent and proof of reparation strategies (few-shot constraints, stronger instruction, or deterministic decoders where available).
[06:33] Nora: we'll also produce error-level examples for failed cases so product teams can triage easily.
[06:38] Omar: back to compliance — audit logs, KMS integration, and retention policy answers needed before we send any production data. I'll circulate a one-page list.
[06:47] Samira: noted — omar you'll send list, we'll respond.
[06:50] Maya: are there any cost expectations for the bench runs? we want a sense of unit economics so our PM can justify it.
[06:57] Samira: initial bench cost estimate will be in the spreadsheet — we break down by tokens, model family, and quantization scenario. we'll give a delta estimate for hosted vs dedicated.
[07:07] Priya: great. any other blockers?
[07:10] Rajiv: IP questions — who owns the golden set and the benchmark results?
[07:14] Samira: standard POC terms — you own your data and golden set; Redwood may use aggregated anonymous performance metrics for product improvement unless you opt out. we'll reflect that in the POC statement of work.
[07:27] Maya: ok that is fine, as long as no raw doc examples leave our bucket.
[07:31] Nora: we'll make sure logs redact PII and raw documents unless explicitly allowed.
[07:36] Samira: wrapping up — recap of commitments and next steps. we'll send the benchmark sheet, setup sandbox, and expect your labeled QA pairs and edge docs early Jan. We'll aim to run the first bench 2027-01-07.
[07:50] Maya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[07:53] Ethan: thanks team. We'll follow up with links: initial spreadsheet (https://redwood.internal/bench/VDG-POC-v1), sandbox docs, and a short template for the golden prompt format.
[08:06] Samira: okay closing, have a good one.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts: 'KV' transcribed sometimes as 'kayvee', model names garbled in spots. Referenced artifacts: benchmark spreadsheet (link above), POC SOW template (link shared post-call).
